overview: The Alternate Fuels for Transportation (Hydrogen Mobility) scheme under the Department of Science & Technology (DST) aims to promote hydrogen as a clean fuel for transportation to reduce carbon emissions and support India's green mobility goals. It focuses on research, development, and deployment of hydrogen-based technologies in the transport sector, including fuel cell vehicles and refueling infrastructure. The scheme supports innovation through funding and collaboration with industry and research institutions to advance hydrogen mobility solutions.
objectives: Promote hydrogen as a clean alternative fuel for transportation
Support research and development in hydrogen fuel cell technologies
Develop hydrogen refueling infrastructure across India
Encourage private sector participation in hydrogen mobility projects
Reduce carbon emissions in the transport sector through green mobility solutions
Align with national goals of Atmanirbhar Bharat and sustainable development
eligibility: Eligible Technology Entities engaged in developing RDI-intensive technology (TRL4 and above), including companies registered under the Companies Act 2013, partnerships under the Indian Partnership Act 1932, limited liability partnerships under the Limited Liability Partnership Act 2008, and startups as defined by DPIIT Notification G.S.R. 127(E) dated 19 February 2019, as may be modified from time to time.
benefits: Financial support through equity, debt, or a combination via Second Level Fund Managers (SLFMs); access to the Research Development and Innovation Fund (RDIF) under the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF); support for scale-up of hydrogen mobility technologies; facilitation of fund flow through Treasury Single Account (TSA) system; intellectual property rights vest with the Eligible Technology Entities.
financial_support: Funding is provided through the Research Development and Innovation Fund (RDIF) with a total outlay of ₹1 lakh crore. Modes of financing include long-term loans at low or nil interest rates, equity infusion (especially for startups), and contributions to Deep-Tech Fund of Funds. Financing can cover up to 50% of assessed project cost for transformative RDI projects at Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) 4 and above, with exceptions possible via the Empowered Group of Secretaries (EGoS). Disbursements are routed exclusively through designated Second-Level Fund Managers (SLFMs).
application_process: 1. Industry stakeholders seeking funding must not send proposals directly to DST. 2. Disbursements are routed exclusively through designated Second-Level Fund Managers (SLFMs). 3. Interested SLFMs (Alternate Investment Funds, Development Finance Institutions, NBFCs, or Focused Research Organizations) must express interest by writing to Dr Jyoti Sharma, Head, RDI Cell at sharma[dot]jyoti[at]nic[dot]in. 4. Existing NBFCs planning to establish AIFs are encouraged to contact DST regarding potential participation. 5. Fund flow from RDIF to SLFMs occurs via Alternate Investment Fund (AIF) mechanisms or loans at low rates with extended tenors. 6. SLFMs prepare fund requirement showing estimated receipts from repayment or exit proceeds and forward to RDIF. 7. Upon receipt of demand, RDIF releases funds to the designated bank account of the SLFM within a specified time frame.
implementing_agency: Department of Science & Technology (DST), Ministry of Science and Technology
caveats: Grants and short-term loans are not supported under the RDI scheme
All disbursements are routed exclusively through designated Second-Level Fund Managers (SLFMs)
Industry stakeholders must not send proposals or emails directly to DST
RDIF shall have to return the entire fund to the Consolidated Fund of India only after 50 years, without any interest
